answer: The ledger seals a prompt each epoch, broadcasts a signal, and opens a 90-second window; answers stamped outside it are dropped. Mid-window the client fetches a fresh nonce and returns it, so a session must be live, not pre-written. It logs the delta between seal and first keystroke and rejects anything under 400 ms. One answer per session per window: a thousand clones need a thousand operators at the same second, and at $0.50 a seat, four a day, a farm burns $2,000 daily before grading. Photographic pigment sets only while light falls on it; a warehouse of unexposed paper stays blank.
